# dutree

dutree displays disk usage as a tree and helps you understand which files and
directories consume space.

Features

 - Coloured output, following the LS_COLORS environment variable (can be
   disabled for ASCII-only output).
 - Display the file system tree with sizes for files and directories.
 - Aggregate small files to simplify the view.
 - Exclude files or directories using patterns.
 - Compare different directories to spot differences in usage.

Usage

```
$ dutree --help
Usage: dutree [options] <path> [<path>..]

Options:
    -d, --depth [DEPTH] show directories up to depth N (def 1)
    -a, --aggr [N[KMG]] aggregate smaller than N B/KiB/MiB/GiB (def 1M)
    -s, --summary       equivalent to -da, or -d1 -a1M
    -u, --usage         report real disk usage instead of file size
    -b, --bytes         print sizes in bytes
    -f, --files-only    skip directories for a fast local overview
    -x, --exclude NAME  exclude matching files or directories
    -H, --no-hidden     exclude hidden files
    -A, --ascii         ASCII characters only, no colors
    -h, --help          show help
    -v, --version       print version number
```
